sections.content: How many people are "precision instrument makers and repairers"?

11,180 people

were counted on the census as "precision instrument makers and repairers" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Precision instrument makers and repairers make, calibrate, test and repair precision and optical instruments such as barometers, compasses, cameras, calibrators, watches, clocks and chronometers.

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "precision instrument makers and repairers" there were more men than women (90.8% compared with 9.2%).

This means "precision instrument makers and repairers" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "skilled metal, electrical and electronic trades".

Men made up 90.8% and women made up 9.2% of "precision instrument makers and repairers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "precision instrument makers and repairers" included:

  • engineering technicians
  • metal making and treating process operatives
  • train and tram drivers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

People who had this job were generally similar in age to the working population

The occupation of "precision instrument makers and repairers" had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 55 to 59 years. Of the whole working population 10.4% were aged 55 to 59 years. For people working as "precision instrument makers and repairers", 11.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "precision instrument makers and repairers" was 16 to 19 years.

  • chartered surveyors
  • artists
  • pipe fitters

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

We can look at who worked as "precision instrument makers and repairers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Among those aged 50 years and older, we see there is a higher proportion of men with this occupation than women.

The percentage of men and women who are "precision instrument makers and repairers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "precision instrument makers and repairers", 9% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a similar age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (86.5% compared with 13.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (84.4%) than self-employed (15.6%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Redcar and Cleveland, this is in the region of the North East.
